text:
whenever i’ve felt stressed, anxious or overwhelmed lately,

i zoom out and remind myself all i have to be grateful for.

we will never have a shortage of problems, they are omnipresent. equally, we should never have a shortage of gratitude.
the lowest friction way to stay motivated is in anticipation. plan dinner with a friend. book a trip. see your parents next weekend. after all, what are we doing this all for?
what others might think of me is the worst measure to decide if something has to be done or not

“i wish i could still do that”

when my 70 year old neighbour said that to me as i was running by and wishing her a good morning, i couldn’t help but feel a sense of pity

if anything, it was a reminder that we’re the youngest we’ll ever be. what’s the point if we don’t take full advantage of it?

our generation lacks the courage we need to be fulfilled

be delusional, what’s the worst that could happen?

“I think it’s a real weakness to want to be liked” - Elon Musk in the Book of Elon

what would you do if you knew it would have no repercussions on your social “image”?
how do you one thing is how you do everything

the secret to productivity

is having the discipline to start

write 1 sentence. run 1 mile.

don't pressure yourself into being motivated
remember, you can reset whenever you want. forget what has happened. focus on what can happen. write down where you are, where you want to be and how you'll get there.

the courage to be disliked. let go of that person inside you that craves external validation. you are not responsible for how others judge you; that is their "task," not yours. what would you do if you knew it would have no repercussions on what people think of you? ok screw that, why haven't you done it?
how lucky are you to be able to read this right now? have food on your plate and a roof over your head. we got lucky. make the most of it!

elite athletes were the first exposure I had to the relentless mindset.

winning without compromise. dedication to your craft.

kobe bryant would be dripping in sweat by the time his teammates showed up to practice. once shot free throws with a torn achilles to tie the game and walked off the court. mentally broke his opponents down before his unparalleled physical preparation completed the job.

Everything negative - pressure, challenges, is all an opportunity for me to rise

- Kobe "Bean" Bryant

i've had this poster in my room for the last 3 years and everyday it reminds me about the dedication it takes to be great.

how you make the customer feel before they even use the product determines their purchasing decision. a high quality product keeps them loyal. from apple's flagship retail stores, to the sensory unboxing experience and the minimalist advertisements create this feeling of intuition and status that sells their products for them.

i think balance is for people who don't know why they're here

- blake crouch, in his book recursion

to read something like that in a random sci-fi book caught me massively off guard, almost making me feel uncomfortable.

if you're seeking your purpose, or lucky enough to have found it, why wouldn't you chase after it? you don't need time away from the thing that drives you…it doesn't feel natural. don't feel guilty for pursuing it relentlessly; go as you are

the more i stare into space, get lost in a book or conversation, the more human i feel

we weren't designed to be constantly task switching, stimulating our brain as fast as our fingers can keep up

Remember, over-explaining is just a way the incompetent attempt to escape. Communicate with few words, clear structure and obvious intent.

The best example of this is Richard Fenyman. Worth watching one of his lectures on YouTube.

you don't need more time,

you need more focus

the internet makes me feel like i'm behind in EVERYTHING

you're not fit enough
you don't eat well enough
you don't travel enough
you don't work hard enough
reminding myself and anyone reading this that the internet is a one-sided facade. no one shows you their failures, sacrifices or dark moments. run your own race!

if someone followed you around for a week, would they believe you're serious about your goals? - grace beverley, founder and CEO of TALA

this really hit me

if your actions don't reflect your goals, they aren't goals - they're just words

asking dumb questions is the best way to unlock huge gains

let your ego go, and let your mind grow
how much more would we appreciate life and the people around us if the internet had a curfew?

when you're born, you look like your parents. when you die, you look like your decisions

you construct the life you live, brick by brick, day by day. make sure you're building what you want

how many times have you stopped yourself from doing something in fear of embarrassment?

if future you might thank you for this, why do you even care about what people think?

it's better to appear as strange to others than be a stranger to yourself

trying to get addicted to mindlessly staring into space while waiting - queues, restaurants, the tube

time feels meaningful when i'm not checking my phone at every opportunity

it's an incredible feeling to face all your fears

- hykeem jamaal carter jr. (aka baby keem)

there's no feeling like staring fear in the face and doing it anyway
The more I read the more I realise how much room for improvement my writing has. It's amazing how well people can string together the 26 letters we have.

When's the last time you intentionally spoke to a stranger? Without any incentive?

It's insane how different all of our lives are. A crazy conjugation of our childhood, culture and circumstances. We can learn something from everyone, isn't that what life is meant to be about?

Why is it so normalised to consume? To scroll your mind away everyday? Why isn't it as normalised to create? Share your ideas with the world - leave it in a better place than you found it.

"Try to be useful. Do useful things for your fellow human beings and the world. It's hard to be useful, to contribute more than you consume. Can you have a positive net contribution to society? Aim for that."

- Elon Musk, as quoted by Eric Jorgensen in The Book of Elon

90% of all online content in 2026 is…….AI-generated. Human attention, one of the most valuable currencies in the world is being swallowed by it. On the flip side, there is a real thirst for human-generated content, driven by a desire for authenticity and the "messiness" that defines the human experience, which AI can't replicate. That's why storytelling and articulation are becoming the most important skills: speak with a structure in mind, use sharp language and concise phrasing, while pronouncing each word like it matters.

Do you remember the last news article, Youtube video or Instagram Reel you watched? Yeah, neither do I. Humans are cognitively wired to learn by doing, so why are we addicted to consuming? Why does it actually feel productive to passively consume? Because it's SO easy.

Experiential learning is defined as learning by doing, through discovery and exploration, followed by critical reflection. It's hard to do something new, with the fear of failure breathing down your neck. But who cares! Do it, fail, get up, learn, and go again. I encourage you to break mould your brain is in, leave your comfort zone and create!
